item.title: Version 3.10.0
item.description:
neoloopy 3.10.0 (build 62)

Scope

  • macOS. This release ships the macOS app (DMG and Sparkle update) with the embedded neoloopy CLI and MCP server. Windows, Linux and Android builds are not part of this release, and the iOS app is not part of this cut.
  • Apple silicon is the native slice of the macOS app. The app is universal; on an Intel Mac the x86_64 slice runs.

In the app

  • See where a Graph node came from. The right pane of a Graph Model shows a node's provenance: what produced it, its identifier and kind there, what that origin said, when it was captured, and the documents behind it with their section, quote and link. A node without a record says "No source recorded."
  • Annotate any node in place. The pane's Notes field writes to the node's own section of the graph note, idea and reference nodes alike, with no modal. What a source said and what you think stay separate: a note never overwrites provenance. A note that cannot be saved stays in the field, or goes to the clipboard if the node was removed meanwhile.
  • Focus fills the canvas. Focus, Show everything and every other canvas start spread the working set to the viewport the way Spread out does on a causal-loop diagram, keep the focused node centred, and reframe on resize until you take the camera. F frames the whole set again.
  • A damaged model explains itself. The Models list keeps a model whose note cannot be read as a row that names the notes to repair, instead of hiding it.
  • Impact Health names what it could not search. A health check on a link edit skips a damaged sibling model, lists it under corpus not searched with the path and reason, and still reviews the model you are editing.

Upgrading from 3.9.1

  • Rebuild the search index before the first read. Run neoloopy index build: the analyzer identity is now +lexical-identifiers.v2+compat-fold.v1, and an older index reports index_stale until rebuilt.
  • Keep document gates open while rebuilding. For a vault serving ingested documents, use LOOPY_PETRI=1 LOOPY_INGEST=1 on the build and subsequent reads; a closed-gate rebuild indexes stubs and reports any shrink.
  • Rebuild older local vectors explicitly. With LOOPY_EMBED_LOCAL_MODEL configured, run neoloopy index build --provider local once to record the token window, prefixes and long-text policy; later rebuilds reuse unchanged vectors with matching identity.
  • Refresh older parses when wanted. ingest-status reports outdated or unknown parser identities; ingest-reparse --dry-run previews an explicit refresh, and ingest-reparse publishes it through the existing pipeline, deferring unavailable parsers with their reasons.

Search and citations

  • Search Graph records. recall and retrieve search node provenance, source quotes and notes; graph hits carry a node anchor and lines: null.
  • Read and walk Graph Models. graph-list, graph-query, graph-edges and graph-node provide vocabulary, filters, negation, facets, batches and bounded paths; Graph authoring remains in the app.
  • Read the cited passage. passage <unit_id> returns indexed text, context and an outline with explicit cuts; it requires an existing fresh index and never builds one.
  • Retrieve several sections. --sections 1..10 defaults to 3, with separately citable passage ids; reranking selects passages before grouping them into document rows.
  • Scope before ranking. --within, --folder, --kind, --model, --match and --not-match constrain candidate selection before lexical, dense and rerank stages; unknown scopes and literal misses are named.
  • Continue after a small budget. ranked.next_offset advances by hits actually emitted, and an empty page keeps its offset until the budget is raised; displaced and omission counts explain graph spreading and trimming.
  • Find identifiers. Section numbers and connector codes have separate fields; identifier headings use the leaf section, while word headings retain ancestor context.
  • Follow a finding. retrieve --expand adds live graph neighbours; reason-with and retrieve.reason_with point to authored causal, process or game connections and exact available reads without running a simulation or diagnosis.

Dense retrieval and reranking

  • Configure dense retrieval. Use LOOPY_EMBED_LOCAL_MODEL locally, or explicitly configure LOOPY_EMBED_URL, LOOPY_EMBED_MODEL and optional LOOPY_EMBED_KEY; --ranking and --provider choose the first stage.
  • Choose local embedding coverage. LOOPY_EMBED_LONG_TEXT=head|mean keeps head as default; mean reads overlapping windows, and policy changes require an explicit vector rebuild.
  • Configure reranking separately. Use LOOPY_RERANK_LOCAL_MODEL, or explicitly configure LOOPY_RERANK_URL, LOOPY_RERANK_MODEL and optional LOOPY_RERANK_KEY; --rerank auto|local|remote|none and --rerank-top select the stage and pair budget.
  • Read long passages. LOOPY_RERANK_LONG_TEXT=first_and_best blends first and best windows by default; head and max_window remain selectable, and identifier mode uses head scoring with tier-first selection and a hard two-text cap per document.
  • Check what ran. Replies expose lexical, dense and rerank stages, coverage and degradation; local failure never silently sends text to a remote provider.
  • Defaults remain unchanged by mock labels. No embedder or reranker model is selected for the host, and the embedding policy stays head; illustrative evaluations report verdict: withheld until expert labels support adoption.

Read reliability and MCP

  • A damaged note costs its own model. Listings retain unavailable; healthy vault-wide reads continue with corpus_not_searched paths and reasons, while targeted damaged-model reads and whole-vault Engage evidence refuse.
  • Treat retrieved text as data. The shared RAG read set projects invisible characters and literal escape prefixes reversibly once on CLI and MCP; decode once to reconstruct source text, preserving notices and omission fields.
  • Send modern MCP metadata. Requests using revision 2026-07-28 require _meta: {"protocolVersion":"2026-07-28","clientCapabilities":{}}; supported legacy clients use initialize.
  • Correct invalid arguments. Known-tool argument mistakes return actionable isError: true results; unknown tools and malformed protocol requests remain protocol errors.
